title: Devapo tests the claims-processing hypothesis rather than the sovereignty one
content:
Devapo is the lead that tests the other hypothesis. It is Camunda-certified with 7+ years in banking, finance and insurance, and small enough to move quickly, but it is UK finance rather than sovereign public sector. An engagement here exercises the claims-processing argument rather than the digital-sovereignty argument.

That is a feature of the lead set rather than a defect in the lead. Most of the Camunda and Common Ground names support the same story: European public bodies needing verifiable records under their own control. Devapo has the same orchestration gap without the sovereignty motive, so it isolates whether the append-only-record pitch stands on operational grounds alone — audit, dispute and replay inside claims handling — with the sovereignty framing removed.

Its size helps that test. A small firm can run a pilot on a decision rather than a procurement, so the hypothesis gets exercised cheaply. It sits at priority 3 because it is a test of the argument rather than a route into the primary market.
